title: USDA Is Cracking Down on Organic Fraud. Will It Rebuild Public Trust?
summary: Article on USDA's Strengthening Organic Enforcement rule, prompted by imported and domestic grain fraud that depressed prices for honest organic farmers.

assertions.quote: falsely labeled organics from Eastern Europe that then began to make their way to the U.S.
“cheap — and fraudulent — organic imports” of corn and soybeans intended as livestock feed
fraudulently expanding the supply of organic feed grain (or anything, for that matter) will depress the prices
Any inspection, however principled the investigator, is likely to be cursory

verdicts.note: Inspection depth varies by certifier and inspector, and there is no systematic measure of how thorough organic inspections are.

assertions.quote: traders, importers, some warehouses, distributors, and brokers, for example, will all have to seek organic certification now

verdicts.note: The rule took effect in 2024 and requires certification of most handlers plus import certificates; its effect on fraud rates is not yet measured.

SOE covers several known gaps: it brings uncertified importers, traders and brokers under oversight, requires electronic import certificates for all organic imports, and adds traceability audits and fraud-prevention plans; this is the agency describing its own rule, with no data on whether fraud fell.

assertions.quote: premium prices that can be 50 percent higher than conventional
